settings.locked.hint: Change it where it is set: an environment variable wins over this page.

settings.restart.body: Saved, and used from the next start: {{list}}. Until then the server keeps its current values.
settings.confirmRestart.title: Save and apply at the next restart?
settings.confirmRestart.body: These settings take effect when the server restarts. If it can't start with them (a port already in use, a certificate it can't get), put the old values back in config.yaml in the data folder.
settings.general.name: Server name
settings.general.nameBody: Shown in the apps when someone connects, on invites and in this console. Leave it empty for AudioSilo.
settings.general.public_urlBody: The address people use from outside your home, used in invite links and QR codes. Leave it empty to use whatever address the browser used.
settings.general.lan_urlBody: The address devices use on your home network, e.g. http://192.168.1.20:8080. The apps switch to it by themselves when they can reach it. Leave it empty to use the address the browser used when it is a home-network address.
settings.general.historyBody: Each listening session records the device and app it was on and the time of day. After this many days that detail is dropped and the session is added into daily totals per person and book, which the Activity pages keep.
settings.general.session_daysBody: From 30 to 3650. The default, 400, keeps a full year of detail for the Activity pages. A change applies at the server's next daily tidy-up.
settings.updates.title: Updates
settings.general.update_checkBody: Once a day the server asks GitHub Releases for the newest version. Only the request itself is sent (your server's address and its version); nothing about your library or people.
settings.updates.offBody: The server no longer contacts GitHub.
settings.network.httpsBody: How this server proves who it is to browsers and apps.
settings.network.mode.offBody: Plain HTTP. Only behind a reverse proxy that does HTTPS.
settings.network.mode.selfsignedBody: Encrypted, but browsers warn the first time. Fine for a home network.
settings.network.mode.autocertBody: Free trusted certificates, renewed automatically. Needs ports 80 and 443 open to the internet.
settings.network.tls_home_httpBody: The phone apps can't trust a self-signed certificate, so this port also answers plain HTTP to devices on your home network. Anything else is sent to HTTPS. Away from home, the apps need Let's Encrypt or a reverse proxy.
settings.network.tls_hostsBody: One per line, like books.example.com. Each must point at this server.
settings.network.cert.title: Certificate
settings.network.bindBody: The address and port the server listens on, like 0.0.0.0:8080. Change it only if something else uses the port.
settings.network.trusted_proxiesBody: Reverse proxies whose X-Forwarded-For header is believed, one address or range per line. Needed for correct addresses on devices and sessions.
settings.network.cors_originsBody: Other websites allowed to call this server's API, one per line. Usually empty.
settings.players.source.embeddedBody: This build carries the web player, so people can listen in a browser.
settings.players.source.dirBody: Served from the folder below, so people can listen in a browser.
settings.players.source.noneBody: This build has no web player and no player folder is set. The apps still work.
settings.players.web_dirBody: Set in config.yaml (web_dir) or AUDIOSILO_WEB_DIR. Takes effect at the next start.
settings.players.linksBody: Let invite links and QR codes open the installed app directly on your own domain. Only useful with an app build that claims this domain.
settings.players.apple_app_idsBody: Team ID and bundle ID, like ABCDE12345.app.audiosilo, one per line (Universal Links).
settings.players.android_sha256Body: SHA-256 of the app's signing certificate, one per line.
settings.metadata.clear.title: Clear community matches
settings.metadata.clear.body: Removes every value and cover a community match wrote, so the books show as not matched again and can be matched from fresh. Your own edits and uploads stay.
settings.metadata.clear.titleAll: Clear the community matches in every library?
settings.metadata.clear.confirmBody: The books go back to what their tags and folders say. Only matching them again brings the community's values back.
settings.metadata.clear.point.values: Titles, authors, narrators, series, years, descriptions, ASINs, ISBNs and covers a community match wrote are removed.
settings.metadata.clear.point.kept: Your own edits, uploaded covers and identifiers from the books' tags stay.
settings.metadata.clear.point.runs: Match runs, and any review still waiting, are removed too.
settings.metadata.clear.doneBody_one: {{formatted}} book is back to its own metadata.
settings.metadata.clear.doneBody_other: {{formatted}} books are back to their own metadata.
settings.metadata.base_urlBody: The community metadata service. Change it only if you run your own.
settings.metadata.matchingCardBody: How a community match picks between a recording's editions in different stores.
settings.metadata.regionBody: The store you buy from. When a recording sells in several, a match takes this store's ASIN.
settings.transcoding.cardBody: Converts formats browsers can't play (Opus, FLAC and others) to MP3 while someone listens. ffprobe reads lengths, chapters and codecs.
settings.transcoding.missing.ffmpeg: Not found, so books in formats browsers can't play won't play in the web player.
settings.transcoding.missing.ffprobe: Not found, so lengths and chapters come only from the files' tags.
settings.transcoding.how: The server finds ffmpeg and ffprobe when it starts: next to its own program, on the PATH, or downloaded into the data folder. Choose others with the --ffmpeg and --ffprobe options.
settings.demo.cardBody: Hands out throwaway accounts at /web/demo so people can try the player without signing up.
settings.demo.enabledBody: Also sends visitors of the site's front page straight to the demo.
settings.demo.libraryBody: The library every demo account gets.
settings.demo.max_usersBody: 0 means no limit. Leave it empty for the default.
settings.demo.idle_ttlBody: A length of time like 30m, 2h or 24h. Leave it empty for 24h.

settings.backups.scheduleBody: In the server's time zone. A backup missed while the server was off runs when it's back.
settings.backups.keepBody: The oldest scheduled backup goes when a new one is made. Manual backups stay until you delete them.
settings.backups.dirBody: Set in config.yaml (backups.dir) or AUDIOSILO_BACKUP_DIR. Copy backups to another disk now and then: a backup on the same disk as the server dies with it.
backups.why.title: The library index can be rebuilt. Your people's data can't.
backups.why.body: A backup is the server's database: accounts, progress, bookmarks, notes, metadata edits, shares, invites, devices and history. Books are read again from your folders after a restore. Settings in config.yaml aren't included.
backups.empty.title: No backups yet
backups.empty.next: The first scheduled backup runs {{when}}. Or back up now.
backups.empty.off: Scheduled backups are off. Back up now, or choose a schedule above.
backups.keepNote: Backups hold every account's password hashes: keep downloaded copies somewhere safe.
backups.failure.disk_full: The disk is full. Free some space; the next backup runs on schedule.
backups.failure.permission_denied: The server can't write to its backups folder. Check the folder's permissions.
backups.failure.failed: See Server > Logs for the cause.
backups.restore.title: Restore this backup?
backups.restore.body: When the server next starts, its database goes back to how it was on {{when}}: accounts, progress, bookmarks, edits, shares, invites and devices. Anything done since is lost.
backups.restore.point.copy: A copy of the current database is made first, so this can be undone by restoring that copy.
backups.restore.point.devices: Devices set up after this backup will need to sign in again.
backups.restore.point.config: Settings in config.yaml stay as they are.
backups.restore.scheduledBody: Restart AudioSilo to apply it. Until then nothing changes.
backups.restore.pendingTitle: A restore is waiting for a restart
backups.restore.pendingBody: When AudioSilo next starts it restores {{name}}, after keeping a copy of the current database. {{who}} asked for it on {{when}}.
backups.restore.doneBody: The database it replaced was kept as {{copy}}.
backups.restore.doneNoCopy: There was no database to keep a copy of.
backups.restore.failure.missing: The backup was gone when the server started. Nothing was changed.
backups.restore.failure.unusable: The backup turned out to be damaged. Nothing was changed.
backups.restore.failure.newer: The backup was made by a newer AudioSilo server. Update this one, then try again. Nothing was changed.
backups.restore.failure.failed: Something went wrong. Nothing was changed; see Server > Logs for the cause.
backups.delete.title: Delete this backup?
backups.delete.body: The backup from {{when}} is deleted from the server's folder. Copies you downloaded aren't affected.
notify.targetsBody: The same events always show in the bell at the top of this console.

notify.empty.body: Send alerts to a webhook (Home Assistant, n8n...), an ntfy topic on your phone, or a Discord channel.
notify.privacy: Alerts carry names, counts and versions. Never a password, code, address or anything that lets someone in. Discord mentions are switched off, so a book title can't ping anyone.
notify.delete.title: Delete {{name}}?
notify.delete.body: Alerts stop going there. You can add it again any time.
notify.toast.addedBody: Send a test to check it works.
notify.kind.webhookBody: A JSON POST to any address, signed if you add a secret.
notify.kind.ntfyBody: Push notifications on your phone through an ntfy topic.
notify.kind.discordBody: A message in a channel, through the channel's webhook.

imports.intro.title: Bring listening history over from Audiobookshelf
imports.intro.what: Copies each person's listening sessions with their real dates and times, how far they got in each book, when they finished, and their bookmarks. Their stats, calendar and year in listening then include it. You review each person's import before anything is written, and an applied import can be undone.
imports.intro.match: Books are matched by file path first, so it works best when Audiobookshelf and AudioSilo read the same folders; then by ASIN or ISBN, then by title and author. Books that don't match are listed and skipped: add them to a library, then import again.

setup.finishedBody: Everything you chose can be changed in Settings and Libraries. Skipped steps wait on Overview.
setup.restartBody: Restart AudioSilo to use the new value. Until then the server keeps its current one.
setup.step.folder.title: Where are your books?
setup.step.folder.why: The folder on the server that holds your audiobooks. AudioSilo checks it's there and readable and shows what it finds, before anything is added.
setup.step.naming.title: How are your books named?
setup.step.naming.why: Book details can come from the files' tags or from the folder names. This decides every book's title, author and series, and changing it later re-reads the whole library.
setup.step.metadata.title: Community metadata
setup.step.metadata.why: Descriptions, series and covers from the community metadata service. Its lookups are the server's main outbound traffic, so it's your choice. Your library is added when you continue.
setup.step.reach.title: How will people reach the server?
setup.step.reach.why: Invite links and pairing QR codes are built from these addresses. A wrong one is the usual reason a phone can't connect.
setup.step.abs.title: Coming from Audiobookshelf?
setup.step.abs.why: Bring your listening progress across, so nobody starts their books again.
setup.step.backups.title: Backups and updates
setup.step.backups.why: A daily copy of the database (listening progress, edits, accounts) and a daily check for new versions.
setup.step.phone.title: Connect a phone
setup.step.phone.why: Scan the code with your phone to start listening, signed in as you.
setup.step.bridge.title: Add a Bridge
setup.step.bridge.why: Optional. A Bridge is a companion container for the jobs the server doesn't do itself.
setup.folder.label: Books folder
setup.folder.hint: The path as the server sees it. In Docker, that's the path inside the container (the right-hand side of the volume, like /audiobooks).
setup.folder.requiredOrSkip: Type the folder that holds your books, or skip this step to add a library later.
setup.folder.error.path_not_absolute: Type the whole path, starting from the top, like /audiobooks or C:\Audiobooks.
setup.folder.error.folder_unreadable: {{root}} isn't there, or the server can't read it. In Docker, type the folder inside the container (the right-hand side of the volume), not the one on your computer, and check the container's user can read it.
setup.folder.error.root_overlaps: {{root}} overlaps a podcast library's folder. Choose a folder that isn't inside it and doesn't contain it.
setup.folder.capped: The check stopped early in a large folder, so there are at least this many.
setup.folder.emptyBody: Check this is the folder that holds your books. In Docker, it's the path inside the container.
setup.folder.sameRootBody: Adding it again makes a second library with the same books. Continue only if that's what you want.
setup.folder.name: Library name
setup.folder.nameHint: Shown in the apps and this console. You can rename it later.
setup.naming.noneBody: Add a books folder in the step before, or skip this: a library added later asks the same question.
setup.naming.previewFailed: Couldn't read sample books from this folder
setup.naming.noSamples: No books to show from this folder.
setup.naming.summary: Blank fields: {{tags}} from tags, {{path}} from folders.
setup.naming.field.title: Title
setup.naming.field.author: Author
setup.naming.absHint: This book has an Audiobookshelf metadata.json, which is read over both.
setup.naming.pick.tags: Best when your files are tagged well (most bought audiobooks are). Folder names fill what the tags leave empty.
setup.naming.pick.path: Best when your folders follow Author / Series / 01 - Title. Tags fill what the folders leave empty.
setup.naming.hint.path: Folder names look more complete for these books.
setup.naming.hint.tags: Tags look more complete for these books.
setup.naming.reresolve_one: Continuing re-reads the details of its {{formatted}} book now. Your own edits stay.
setup.naming.reresolve_other: Continuing re-reads the details of its {{formatted}} books now. Your own edits stay.
setup.naming.switched: {{name}} now reads its book details another way
setup.metadata.toggleBody: Players show the extra details only while this is on. Off, nothing about your books leaves the server for it.
setup.metadata.regionBody: The store you buy from. The wrong one matches books to the wrong edition.
setup.metadata.creates: Continuing adds {{name}} and starts its first scan, with these choices.
setup.metadata.scanning: Its first scan has started. You can carry on while it runs.
setup.reach.browser: This browser reaches the server at
setup.reach.seenAs: The server sees this page at {{address}}: something in between, like a reverse proxy, changed the address.
setup.reach.publicBody: The address that works from anywhere, used in invites and QR codes. Leave it empty to use whatever address the browser used.
setup.reach.lanBody: The address on your home network, like http://192.168.1.20:8080. The apps switch to it when they can reach it.
setup.reach.proxy: A reverse proxy is in front of the server
setup.reach.proxyBody: Requests reach the server from {{peer}}, which isn't a trusted proxy yet. Trust it so sessions and devices show each person's real address.
setup.reach.phones.off: Plain HTTP. Phones connect at home; away from home, put a reverse proxy with HTTPS in front, or switch to Let's Encrypt.
setup.reach.phones.selfsigned: Browsers warn the first time, and the phone apps can't trust a self-signed certificate: at home they use plain HTTP (below); away from home they need Let's Encrypt or a reverse proxy.
setup.reach.phones.autocert: A trusted certificate: phones and browsers connect from anywhere without a warning.
setup.abs.body: AudioSilo can read your Audiobookshelf server's listening progress and bring it across for each person.
setup.abs.import: The import is in Settings > Import: connect to Audiobookshelf, review what matches, then apply it. It can be undone.
setup.abs.metadata: Your folders' metadata.json files from Audiobookshelf are read as they are: titles, authors, series and descriptions come across with the books.
setup.backups.dirBody: Set in config.yaml (backups.dir) or AUDIOSILO_BACKUP_DIR. Copy backups to another disk now and then.
setup.phone.qr: Pairing QR code for your phone
setup.phone.scanBody: It opens the AudioSilo app, or the web player, signed in as you. The code works once, for ten minutes.
setup.phone.failed: Couldn't make a pairing code. Try a new one.
setup.phone.webBody: In a new tab, signed in as you.
setup.phone.ffmpeg: ffmpeg is ready: books in formats a browser can't play are converted as they stream.
setup.phone.noFfmpeg: No ffmpeg: books in formats a browser can't play won't play in the web player. Install ffmpeg on the server to fix it.
setup.phone.household: Sharing with family? Each person can add household members from Me > Household in the player.
setup.bridge.about: A Bridge runs beside the server and does the work the server won't: it writes to your library folders and runs heavy jobs like generated character sheets and recaps, so the server itself stays read-only. The server never connects to it; once paired, the Bridge calls in.
setup.bridge.composeIntro: Add it to the compose file that runs the server:
setup.bridge.agent: For characters and recaps, also add the agent container from the Bridge's README.
setup.bridge.online: A Bridge is paired and online
